scenes.head: It can't write a word
scenes.say: Google just launched an AI that cannot write a single word. So why does it matter?

scenes.head: 1 input. 1,000 questions.
scenes.say: It's the Gemini Decisions API. You give it one input, and up to a thousand questions.

scenes.head: Three kinds of answers
scenes.say: Yes or no. Pick one. Or score it. And every answer comes with a confidence number.

scenes.head: A very fast sorting clerk
scenes.say: Picture a very fast sorting clerk. Is this email a complaint? Which team gets it? And how sure is it?

scenes.head: Fast and cheap
scenes.say: Google says it answers in about one hundred fifty to two hundred fifty milliseconds. And it costs ten cents per million input tokens, with nothing for output.

scenes.head: Here's the catch
scenes.say: Here's the catch. Every benchmark number comes from Google itself.

scenes.head: It doesn't win everywhere
scenes.say: Google says it leads seven of nine. A rival called Jev wins the other two, and it's cheaper.

scenes.head: Pros and cons
scenes.say: The good: numbers instead of sentences, and it reads audio, video and PDFs. The bad: it's not the cheapest, it can't be self-hosted, and it can't write text.

scenes.head: Who it's for
scenes.say: So who is it for? Teams making the same small decision thousands of times a day.

scenes.head: Full breakdown on my blog
scenes.say: Full pros and cons, with sources, are on my blog. Follow for a new AI tool every day.
